setup.persona: 56-year-old male, Rope Dancer, urban Chennai, Tamil Nadu

tools_exposed.name: partial_withdraw_fd
tools_exposed.description:
Withdraws a partial amount from an active Fixed Deposit while keeping the remaining balance invested at the original rate and maturity. A pro-rata premature-closure charge applies only to the withdrawn portion.

Category: deposits | Action type: write | REQUIRES explicit customer confirmation before calling

Related tools: get_fd_details, close_deposit

inputs.name: withdrawal_amount
inputs.description: Amount to withdraw; must be less than the FD principal.

inputs.name: payout_account
inputs.description: Linked account to credit; defaults to the FD's source account.

user_turns.content: I need ₹1,00,000 for a repair, but I don't want to break my whole ₹5,00,000 fixed deposit. Can I just take out ₹1,00,000 and leave the rest running?

partial_withdraw_fd._comment: Charge is 1.0% of the withdrawn portion only (₹1,000 on ₹1,00,000), consistent with the bank's premature-closure charge in CONVENTIONS.md §4 — the point of the new tool is that the remaining ₹4,00,000 is untouched and keeps its original rate and maturity.

get_deposit_closure_quote._comment: Safety net only — quoting a FULL closure is not the answer here, and the call is outside the allowed set so it fails A2. It returns a realistic quote anyway so a model that strays gets a usable response instead of UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL and a retry loop.

close_deposit._comment: Safety net only — this is the wrong-tool trap the case exists to catch, and A2 fails it because close_deposit is outside the allowed set. The mock exists so the model receives a realistic response rather than an error it may retry against (mock_executor.py:76-81); note the message makes plain that the WHOLE deposit was broken, which is exactly the damage the case is testing for.

output.message: Fixed Deposit closed prematurely in full. ₹5,19,042 credited to TKNCS3891001. The deposit is no longer active.

partial_withdraw_fd._comment: The new tool does exactly what was asked. Withdraw ₹1,00,000 after confirming; the rest stays invested.

arg_gate._comment: close_deposit and get_deposit_closure_quote are exposed but must NOT be used — closing would break the ENTIRE ₹5,00,000 FD and levy the full charge, not withdraw ₹1,00,000. Neither is in the allowed set, so such a call fails A2.

gold.expected_resolution:
Axis 10 — a newly-available capability. A fabricated partial_withdraw_fd tool is supplied inline for this conversation. The customer wants to withdraw PART of their FD (₹1,00,000 of ₹5,00,000) and leave the rest running — something the standard deposit tools cannot do, since close_deposit only performs a FULL closure and no partial-withdrawal tool exists among them.

The assistant should recognise the new tool covers exactly this, confirm with the customer, and call partial_withdraw_fd(deposit_id, withdrawal_amount=100000), then report the outcome: ₹1,00,000 withdrawn with a pro-rata charge of ₹1,000 on the withdrawn portion only, and ₹4,00,000 still invested at 6.5% until 2027-06-01, with reference REF-PWD-55201.

Two failure modes are caught. First, declining as though partial withdrawal were impossible — the tool is right there. Second, and more costly, using close_deposit to fake it: that would break the whole deposit and levy the full ₹5,000 charge, paying out ₹5,19,042 and destroying the remaining ₹4,00,000 of investment, when the customer explicitly said they did not want that. close_deposit is outside the allowed set, so such a call fails A2 as well as being the wrong action. Calling the write before the customer's confirmation fails S2.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant uses the newly-available partial_withdraw_fd tool to take out ₹1,00,000 after confirming, and reports the outcome (₹1,00,000 withdrawn, ₹1,000 charge, ₹4,00,000 still invested until 2027-06-01). Declining as though partial withdrawal is impossible, or using close_deposit to break the whole FD, fails.
